label: verify-t4-glide-deep

claims.claim: Terminal descent speed has a minimum at intermediate fold angle KL: about 2.3 at psi=0 and about 1.2 at psi=35 (data: 0.1011 m/s at KL 2.31; 0.0674-0.0676 at KL 1.2-1.33).
claims.source_says: minimum terminal descent velocity is around KL 2.3 ... the optimal fold angle has decreased, with a minimum terminal descent velocity obtained near KL 1.2.
claims.note: Paper text matches both optima; I did not reopen the data file, but the agent's stored script output shows those speeds and the ratio 0.1011/0.0676 is 1.50.

claims.claim: The blade-element model is partly tuned: published drag is halved, model loading 1.2 g differs from data key 2.16 g, and the model psi=0/psi=35 best-speed ratio is 1.21 versus 1.50 in data.
claims.source_says: compared to the results of [52], we reduce the value of the drag coefficient to obtain good agreement with our experiments. ... a net mass loading of 1.2 grams.
claims.note: Drag reduction and 1.2 g are in the paper and 4709/3900=1.207, 0.1011/0.0676=1.496 reproduce, but the paper says only 'reduce' (the factor 2 and the 2.16 g key rest on repo files I did not fully confirm).

claims.claim: Wild whirling fruits have mean fold angle 1.8 (10 percent image error, 27 fruits), at the model optimum for base angle 15 deg; base angle of each fruit not reported.
claims.source_says: error of ~10% [46], which is illustrated by the errorbar from mean(KL) = 1.8 ± 0.18 in Fig. 3. The measured fold angles from wild fruits are enumerated as [1-27]
claims.note: Mean 1.8, 10 percent and 27 fruits are confirmed; the 1.80 model optimum at psi=15 comes from stored repo files I did not re-read, and no per-fruit base angle appears.

claims.claim: The wind-drift bound (wind x height / sink speed) is 4.1-8.0 times (median 6.9) above fitted field distances for dipterocarp fruits.
claims.note: Dividing the ballistic by the LMM column for the 12 species in Smith Table 3 gives 4.15 to 8.05, median 6.86.

overall: Three of the four key claims reproduce from the sources I fetched, with two caveats on partial support. The dispersal-ratio and fold-angle claims are solid. The tuning and wild-fruit claims rely partly on repo model files I did not re-read.
